#

The ghost-gl-adapter-core package provides a framework-agnostic bridge between
host frameworks and ghost-gl-core.


Installation#




createGridHost#

Creates a framework-agnostic grid host:




GridHost API#

PROPERTY       TYPE                 DESCRIPTION
controller     RuntimeController    Core controller
state          GridHostState        Current state snapshot
materialized   MaterializedNode[]   Items to render
isReady        boolean              Initialization complete


Methods#

METHOD                   DESCRIPTION
setViewport(rect)        Update visible viewport
setContainerSize(size)   Update container dimensions
moveNode(id, x, y)       Move item
resizeNode(id, w, h)     Resize item
beginDrag(input)         Start drag interaction
updateDrag(input)        Update drag position
endDrag()                Commit drag
cancelDrag()             Cancel drag
subscribe(listener)      Subscribe to state changes
dispose()                Release resources


Framework Adapters#

Framework adapters (React, Vue, etc.) are thin wrappers around GridHost:

 1. Create GridHost via createGridHost
 2. Wire scroll/layout events to host.setViewport
 3. Wire pointer events to host.beginDrag/updateDrag/endDrag
 4. Subscribe and render host.materialized

title: Introduction
content:
#

Ghost-GL is a high-performance virtualized grid layout engine designed for heavy
components (charts, editors, tables) with mount costs of 10-100ms+.


Why Ghost-GL?#

Traditional virtualized grids assume lightweight items. When items are heavy
(complex charts, rich editors), mounting them all at once causes frame drops.

Ghost-GL solves this with three-state materialization:

 1. Ghost - Placeholder, not rendered
 2. Shell - Minimal render (skeleton, border)
 3. Live - Full component mounted


Key Concepts#


Three-State Materialization#

STATE   DESCRIPTION            USE CASE
ghost   Not rendered           Items far from viewport
shell   Skeleton/border only   Items approaching viewport
live    Full component         Items in viewport


Budget-Driven Scheduling#

Ghost-GL schedules materialization within a 16ms frame budget to maintain 60fps.
Only items that can be fully rendered within the budget are materialized.


Spatial Indexing#

Uses RBush R-tree for O(log n) spatial queries, enabling fast collision
detection and viewport queries even with thousands of items.
